applies_why: The judge text resolves the Luke 2:48 challenge by immediate verse context rather than by chain-against-chain footing, which is what K-C governs when a pressed link is met by the pressing side's own chain read together.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse": (1) the judge may resolve by immediate context within Luke 2:48-49; (2) K-C requires weighing the pressing chain against the defended chain by footing, so intra-verse qualification is not enough.
why: The judge resolves the collision by contrasting Luke 2:48 with Luke 2:49 verse-by-verse instead of weighing the pressing chain against the defended chain by footing, which K-C forbids.
